strongest_angle: Examine the colossal volcanic eruptions of the Turkey Creek caldera 27 million years ago that deposited massive layers of rhyolite tuff, which subsequently eroded into the towering stone spires of Chiricahua National Monument.

key_facts.fact: Chiricahua National Monument in Arizona features prominent rhyolite pinnacles created 27 million years ago by one of the largest known volcanic eruptions in the American Southwest.
Remnants of the Turkey Creek caldera in Arizona provide evidence for successive large volcanic eruptions beginning about 26.9 million years ago.
The sentinel spires and rock formations of Chiricahua National Monument rise hundreds of feet into the air within the Chiricahua Mountains Sky Island Complex.
A massive magma chamber grew just a few miles under the Earth's surface before erupting and spewing more than 100 cubic miles of material.
